business_scope.primary_industry_name: Deep-Sea Tugboat Towage and Maritime Emergency Salvage Contracts

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Colombia (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic) with codified commercial law (Código de Comercio, Decree 410 of 1971) and constitutional supremacy; S.A.S. contractarian flexibility under Law 1258 of 2008
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA, in force 2012) with Investment Chapter
Colombia–European Union Multiparty Trade Agreement (provisionally applied since 2013) with investment protections
Colombia–United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (in force 2021)
Colombia–South Korea Double Taxation Agreement (in force 2019)
Andean Community CAN Decision 578 (Common Investment Regime)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 1258 of 2008 (S.A.S. regime); Law 2155 of 2021 (Article 89) and Decree 830 of 2021 (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales – UBO registry, 5% threshold); Law 526 of 1999 (UIAF); Law 1121 of 2006 (AML/CFT); Decree 83 of 2017 (PEP regulation); Circular 002 of 2023 (UIAF risk-management standard); Circular 2023-100-000015 (Superintendencia de Sociedades on identification of clients, shareholders and UBOs)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the foreign shareholder's certificate of legal existence and good standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry or Chamber of Commerce of the shareholder's domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Colombia party since 01.01.2004) or Consular Legalization if the issuing state is not a Hague Convention member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special power of attorney (poder especial) granted by each foreign founding shareholder to the Colombian incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (non-Hague issuing jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport pages of all founding shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners (natural persons)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent consulate or notary public of the residence country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Official Spanish translation (traducción oficial) of corporate and personal identification documents issued in a non-Spanish language
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator (Traductor Oficial) recognized by the Colombian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of translator's signature plus subsequent authentication chain (Apostille where applicable)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of shareholders, UBOs and authorized signatories against (i) OFAC SDN and consolidated sanctions; (ii) UN Security Council consolidated lists; (iii) EU consolidated financial sanctions; (iv) Colombian Procuraduría and Contraloría ineligibility registries; (v) Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia administrative sanctions; and (vi) terrorist-financing lists under Colombian Law 1621 of 2013. PEP identification follows Decree 83 of 2017. For the medium-risk maritime towage/salvage segment (ISIC 5222), the S.A.S. must adopt risk-based onboarding, enhanced due diligence for escrow and Lloyds-standard wire payment rails, and annual UBO re-certification.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial (RUES) – www.rues.org.co, operated through the local Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá) issuing the Certificado de Homonimia or name-reservation certificate
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Registration language is Spanish only. Under Article 177 of the Código de Comercio and RUES standards, the corporate name must contain a distinctive element (denominación razonada or fantasy word) followed by the mandatory suffix 'S.A.S.'. Non-Spanish or non-Latin-script names must be submitted in an official sworn Spanish transliteration; the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered companies, brands, or the reserved names of third parties.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying official government character: Ministerio, Presidencia, Gobernación, Alcaldía, Nacional, República (prior authorization from Ministerio del Interior required)
Financial-sector terms: Banco, Seguros, Aseguradora, Fiducia, Fondo de Pensiones, Valores, Comisionista (prior license from Superintendencia Financiera required)
Hydrocarbon and mining terms: Petróleos, Gas, Carbón, Minerales, Minería (prior authorization from Ministerio de Minas y Energía required)
Maritime-military references: Armada, Armada Nacional, Capitanía, DIMAR, Submarino (prior authorization from Ministerio de Defensa/DIMAR required)
Terms contrary to public order, health, or morality, or offensive to public institutions
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If RUES/Chamber of Commerce rejects the proposed name, the applicant receives a detailed denial identifying the conflicting token or registry entry. Within 10 working days of notification, file a 'recurso de reposición' with the same Cámara de Comercio and, concurrently or in the alternative, a 'recurso de apelación' before the Superintendencia de Sociedades under Ley 1437 de 2011 (CPACA); judicial review may be pursued before the Administrative Jurisdiction (Jurisdicción Contencioso-Administrativa) within 2 months of the final administrative act. In parallel, the applicant may immediately reserve a new alternative name through RUES without prejudice to the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole registered domicile (domicilio social) of a licensed maritime towage/salvage operator: the Chamber of Commerce, DIAN and DIMAR require an effective, geo-referenced physical address in a Colombian municipality for service of process and vessel oversight. A virtual back-office may support administrative functions only and cannot substitute the statutory seat.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk ~40% within the first 18 months of operation: DIAN carries out geo-referenced inspection visits to verify effective establishment, while DIMAR performs unannounced technical inspections for holders of towage/salvage operating permits; once the vessel license is active, annual inspection is expected.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Stage 1 legal and AML/CFT due-diligence engagement (entity design, OFAC/UN/PEP screening, UBO chart, incorporation docs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark (fixed fee or hourly rate)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and homonymy certificate via RUES
Notarial fees for the public deed of incorporation (escritura pública) and related notarial certifications
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notaría Pública with jurisdiction over the registered seat

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial registration of the S.A.S. and matriculación mercantil
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio (local chamber with territorial jurisdiction)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee of 0.7% on subscribed capital (Ley 1429 de 2010), with absolute caps

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille processing for foreign shareholder/UBO documents (estimated 4 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Dirección de Autenticaciones) of the issuing country

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official sworn Spanish translation of foreign-issued incorporation documents and passports
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Traductor Oficial recognized by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO registry filing (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales) via RUES/DIAN
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: DIAN – Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales / Confecámaras

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: DIMAR pre-consultation and maritime activity feasibility certificate for towage/salvage
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: DIMAR – Dirección General Marítima, Ministerio de Defensa
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Maritime administrative fee schedule (Fondo de Defensa Nacional)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 – Article 5 (S.A.S. incorporation content) and Article 17 (corporate limited liability); Código de Comercio (Decreto-Ley 410 de 1971) Articles 98, 110, 112, 354 (merchant registration and corporate powers); Decreto 1074 de 2015 Articles 2.2.1.1.1–2.2.1.1.9 (RUES digital formalities).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered-office territorial jurisdiction, operating the Registro Único Empresarial (RUES) under the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Tourism.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución de Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada S.A.S. – private written incorporation instrument authenticated before the Chamber of Commerce (or notary only if incorporating real estate or vessels).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum authorized or subscribed capital for a S.A.S.; capital must be stated in the incorporation instrument and subscribed, and any deferred payments must be settled no later than two years under Article 3 of Ley 1258 de 2008. No government escrow account is required; DIMAR separately reviews the financial capacity of the towage/salvage operation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION 001/2025 – First Board Resolution. The Shareholders/Board, acting upon the company’s lawful constitution, unanimously resolves: (1) ratify the full subscription and allocation of shares as set forth in the incorporation instrument; (2) adopt the registered office at Calle 86 No. 10-12, Bogotá D.C., as the sole official domicile for administrative, legal and RUES notices; (3) appoint [Name Surname] as Legal Representative and [Name] as Secretary, with powers per the S.A.S. bylaws; (4) authorize registration before the Chamber of Commerce, NIT/RUT issuance and bank account opening; and (5) instruct management to apply for the DIMAR towage-and-salvage operating permit. Approved unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-reservation and validation of corporate name (homónimo) in the Single Business Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio / Registro Único Empresarial (RUES) – online portal www.rue.com.co
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a RUES name-search and reservation request selecting the jurisdiction of Bogotá D.C.; confirm the denomination is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing entity; obtain the reservation certificate valid for 90 days; include the 'S.A.S.' suffix.
required_dossiers: RUES pre-registration form
Passport or cédula of subscribing shareholder or legal representative
Proof of payment of RUES search fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resubmit with an alternative denomination or appeal the Chamber of Commerce negative similarity decision within 10 business days under Decree 1074 of 2015.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the S.A.S. private incorporation instrument (bylaws and share subscription)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (for signature authentication) and Cámara de Comercio (for registration effect)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statutory instrument under Article 5 of Ley 1258 de 2008: corporate name, purpose (offshore towage and emergency salvage), capital, share classes, governance, profit distribution and facultative arbitration. Have shareholders sign before a notary if the fleet includes registered vessels; otherwise a private instrument suffices.
required_dossiers: Articles of incorporation / bylaws
Share subscription list and proof of capital payment
Written consent of each designated legal representative
Apostilled power of attorney and passport for non-resident shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any formal defect noticed by the Notary or Chamber; re-execute and re-certify the amended instrument within 5 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial registration (Registro Mercantil) of the S.A.S. incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá D.C. (territorial chamber) via RUES
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed incorporation document, RUES registration forms and payment of registry and municipal fees through RUES or a Chamber branch. Upon compliance, the Chamber issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal evidencing formation and the representatives' powers.
required_dossiers: Executed private instrument (original plus copy)
RUES registration forms (Formulario Único de Registro)
DIAN pre-NIT data
Registered-office address authorization (lease or notarized permission)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the examiner raises inconsistencies, file corrective statements twice within 5 business days per Article 2.2.1.1.4 of Decree 1074 of 2015.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NIT issuance, RUT activation and electronic-invoicing enablement at DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN – Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (including online RUT and electronic-invoicing services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the Chamber-issued digital certificate to obtain automatic NIT allocation and update the RUT; enable the Factura Electrónica de Venta (FEV) system and register the economic activity under CIIU code 5222 (towage and salvage maritime services) for correct VAT and income tax positioning.
required_dossiers: Certificado de existencia y representación legal
RUT registration form
Identity documents of legal representatives and shareholders
Proof of registered-office address (public utility bill or lease)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify RUT fields electronically through the DIAN transactional service within 5 business days; escalate to a physical DIAN appointment if the portal rejects the correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate bank account, SWIFT/escrow payment rails and SAGRILAFT anti-money-laundering setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank; UIAF – Unidad de Información y Análisis Financiero (reporting framework)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a dedicated corporate account permitting Lloyd's Standard Form wires and escrow settlements for salvage contracts; complete KYC and PEP verification of shareholders; configure the SAGRILAFT risk management system and appoint an AML officer consistent with the medium-enhanced risk tier.
required_dossiers: Company certificate from Cámara de Comercio
NIT/RUT record
Passport or cédula of legal representatives
Registered-office address proof
Expected transaction volume declaration and AML risk matrix
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises documentary queries, submit the corrected KYC package within 15 days or transfer the application to an alternate regulated bank; UIAF transaction reporting starts only after commercial operations commence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Maritime service-company registration and operating permit before the General Maritime Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIMAR – Dirección General Marítima (National Maritime Authority) and the applicable Capitanía de Puerto
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Chamber certificate and DIMAR application through the SISVIA/Port Captaincy to obtain the towage and salvage maritime service permit; attach the tug fleet flag registration, P&I insurance, salvage-response plan and SOLAS/ISPS security compliance evidence.
required_dossiers: Certificado de existencia y representación legal
NIT/RUT
Vessel ownership, flag and matrícula certificates for tugboats
ISM Code Safety Management Certificate
P&I and H&M insurance certificates with salvage coverage
Environmental and oil-spill contingency plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: DIMAR judicial and administrative notifications are cured under Law 1437 of 2011: present additional documentary evidence within 30 working days; if the permit is denied, file a reposición recourse before DIMAR or an appeal to the Ministry of Defense.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: DIMAR – Dirección General Marítima (Ministry of Defense), assisted by the Superintendencia de Puertos y Transporte for harbor towage activities
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permiso de Prestación de Servicios de Remolque y Salvamento Marítimo (PPSRM) – maritime service-company operating certificate

environmental_impact_assessment.agency_name: ANLA – Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (with regional environmental authority for port-adjacent operations)
environmental_impact_assessment.classification_tier: Category B (medium impact) – environmental management plan and discharge registration; a Full EIA (Estudio de Impacto Ambiental) is mandatory only if the company installs port-side oily-waste reception, bunkering or dock infrastructure.
environmental_impact_assessment.discharge_and_emissions_standards: All tugs must comply with MARPOL Annex I (15 ppm oily-water separator standard and prohibition of discharge within 12 nautical miles), Annex V waste return-to-authorizer handling, Annex VI global sulfur cap of 0.50% m/m; maintain an approved DIMAR discharge and emissions logbook, and ensure hazardous waste is delivered to a licensed gestor under Decree 4741 of 2005.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety technical concept issued by the Cuerpo de Bomberos Oficiales for the office and tug berth; structural-load verification for shore facilities; SG-SST occupational safety and health program per Decreto 1072 de 2015; ARL labor-risk affiliation; DIMAR safety-management endorsement; STCW-certified crews with valid medical and drug-test clearances.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) – official national tax and customs authority; portal: www.dian.gov.co; electronic transactional platform: MUISCA (Modelo Unificado de Ingresos, Servicios Tributarios y Aduaneros) at www.muisca.dian.gov.co.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity intending to operate as a Colombian S.A.S. must: (1) appoint a legal representative or attorney-in-fact domiciled in Colombia; (2) execute the bylaws and register the S.A.S. in the mercantile registry of the competent Cámara de Comercio; (3) obtain the Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation; (4) enroll in the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) before DIAN, thereby obtaining the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria); (5) select all relevant tax obligations in the RUT, including IVA, ICA (industry and commerce tax) and, if applicable, national registration as responsible de IVA; and (6) obtain a valid digital signature (firma electrónica) from a DIAN-authorized certification authority to enable electronic invoicing and MUISCA filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia does not adopt the U.S. check-the-box regime; a S.A.S. is always treated as a juridical person subject to entity-level taxation. Statutory elections available to a qualifying S.A.S. include the optional Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLE, Articles 903–916 E.T.) for eligible small enterprises with gross revenues below 80,000 UVT, and optional customs/export-treatment elections such as inclusion in a permanent or U.T. zone regime when authorized by DIAN and the National Tax and Customs Directorate. Hybrid mismatch elections are not recognized under Colombian tax law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre las Ventas) – national value added tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No economic turnover threshold applies to S.A.S. legal entities; registration as a responsible de IVA in the RUT is mandatory before carrying out any taxable act in Colombia. The regulatory threshold of 1,000 UVT (approx. COP 47,324,000 for tax year 2025) only relieves certain non-merchant natural persons from electronic invoicing obligations, not corporate entities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing (factura electrónica de venta) is mandatory for all S.A.S. taxpayers. Invoices must be generated through DIAN-authorized software or an authorized technology provider, transmitted in real time to DIAN via the MUISCA/RADIAN platform, validated by DIAN's fiscal control system, and accompanied by a digital stamp and electronic signature. Export invoices must include the corresponding foreign-trade documentation number; failure to obtain valid electronic acceptance renders the invoice legally ineffective for VAT deduction and export zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Colombia under the customs regime are VAT zero-rated. For services, zero-rating applies only to services that are 'exported services' as defined by Article 481 E.T.: services rendered by a Colombian IVA-responsible taxpayer to a non-resident recipient with no domicile in Colombia, fully developed in Colombian territory, and benefitting exclusively from abroad. In the context of deep-sea tugboat towage and maritime salvage, the service must be supplied to a foreign principal or operating beyond Colombian territorial waters, and the entire economic benefit must be realized abroad. The exporter must be enrolled in RUT, issue electronic invoices, and retain contractual and payment evidence demonstrating the foreign destination of the service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) filed with DIAN under the Colombian customs statute when vessels or towed equipment physically leave Colombia
Bill of Lading / Sea Waybill evidencing shipment from a Colombian port
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas) or bank intermediary credit certificate evidencing foreign exchange collection
Offshore towage/salvage contract and documentary proof that the recipient is a non-domiciled party and the service is used exclusively abroad
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN may scrutinize export zero-rating claims for 5 years from the tax return due date. Unsupported or fraudulent zero-rating results in retroactive VAT collection, monetary interest, and penalties of up to 200% of the omitted tax under Article 648 E.T. Misrepresentation of an export may also trigger customs sanctions under Decree 1165/2019, loss of VAT refund rights, exclusion from trusted exporter programs, and criminal tax fraud liability under Article 434-A of the Colombian Criminal Code, including imprisonment for the legal representative in egregious cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank), with supervised foreign-exchange information reporting through the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN); banking supervision by Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia operates a free-floating market-based exchange system under the Régimen de Cambios Internacionales (Foreign Exchange Regime). Current account transactions, including towage and salvage service receipts, are fully convertible and may be settled freely, provided they are channeled through an authorized foreign-exchange intermediary when converted into Colombian pesos. Capital account transactions (foreign direct investment inflows, shareholder loans, and outbound investment) are also permitted but require registration with Banco de la República through the foreign-exchange declaration (Formulario No. 12). Profit remittance and dividend payout to non-resident shareholders are lawful without exchange-control approval once the local company has satisfied corporate income tax obligations and the foreign-exchange registration for the underlying FDI is current; however, remittances of pure capital gains absent adequate tax filing may be blocked by DIAN and banking compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For services exports (including deep-sea towage and emergency salvage), the statutory repatriation term is six months from the accrual/performance date. The exporter must channel the foreign-currency proceeds through the mercado cambiario by selling 100% of the collected amount to an authorized bank or broker in local currency, unless the proceeds are eligible for a permitted exception (e.g., prior-authorized maintenance of funds in an offshore operational account for coverage of voyage or salvage-related disbursements). Goods exports are subject to a four-month surrender period. Failure to repatriate or the unauthorised accumulation of foreign currency abroad triggers DIAN exercise of exchange-control surcharges and penalties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account in COP and USD
Operational Account / Escrow for Maritime Contracts

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium (conditional). Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Digital Wallet Platforms, multi-currency IBAN providers) are viable as a secondary collection layer for foreign-currency receivables and for urgent supplier payments outside Colombia, but they are not authorized local FX intermediaries and cannot legally settle Colombian peso-denominated payroll, tax, or social-security obligations. Decree 2555/2010 requires a banking or special authorization for deposit-taking and clearing; therefore any EMI must operate under a partnership with a licensed Colombian bank for COP clearing. EMI transactions trigger enhanced KYC and enhanced sanctions screening, so use them strictly for trade/advance receivables and never for escrow of salvage awards or capital injections.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A mandatory live videoconference KYC interview is required for all legal representatives of the SAS. Most tier-1 banks, including Bancolombia and BBVA, will also request either physical appearance of the legal representative in Bogotá or the appointment of a local registered attorney-in-fact (apoderado) to present original documents. Remote opening is possible for entities incorporated in non-sanctioned jurisdictions, subject to notarised and apostilled constitutional deeds, a certified copy of the RUT, a complete listing of ultimate beneficial owners, and an in-person document inspection by the compliance officer before account activation. Banks with high maritime exposure may additionally require a personal interview with the vessel operator or fleet manager.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk maritime flags, open registries, or frequent operation in piracy-prone or sanctioned-adjacent waters (e.g., Gulf of Aden, Malacca Strait, Somali Basin).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide complete vessel ownership chain with IMO registration, classification society certificates, Port State Control inspection records, AIS and LRIT tracking history for the last 12 months, Lloyds or IUA insurance certificates, environmental compliance documents, a signed warranty that the vessel does not enter UN/EU/OFAC-sanctioned routes, and a detailed voyage schedule with verifiable commercial purposes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border remittances originating from non-bank financial institutions, crypto-adjacent platforms, or unknown overseas third parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver an AML/KYC counter-party dossier consisting of the source of funds statement, the underlying towage/salvage contract, invoice trail matching the remittance amount, the legal opinion of the correspondent bank, a certified list of beneficial owners, and real-time OFAC/EU sanctions-screening results for the receiving entity and its principals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lump-sum equity injections from a non-resident shareholder exceeding the stated registered capital without a clear economic rationale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a notarised board resolution approving the capital contribution, signed shareholder contribution agreement, sworn declaration of origin and legitimacy of funds, audited financial statements of the shareholder, bank statements evidencing the funding source, the FDI registration form (Formulario No. 12), and letter of responsibility executed by the compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent large transfers to crew, local port agents, or bunker suppliers that fall outside standard procurement routines.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the treasury cash-management policy, the crew employment register and payroll schedules, the vessel disbursement accounts ledger, dated service agreements with each port agent and supplier, pre-verified supplier due-diligence files, and U.S. and EU sanctions-control certifications from all payees.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfers for inbound capital injection must be executed via SWIFT MT103/202 from the shareholder's foreign bank to the SAS's Operational Account at an authorized Colombian bank. The remittance instruction must cite the capital contribution purpose code under the Colombian Exchange Regime (Concept Code 1101, Inversión Internacional para Inversión Directa). The receiving bank will generate the mandatory Formulario No. 12 'Declaración de Cambio por Inversión Internacional' prior to conversion to COP and funds availability. The bank also verifies the apostilled corporate documents, RUT, and the registered investment before issuing the 'Registro de Inversión Internacional' certificate from Banco de la República. Local law requires that the capital injection be recorded with the DIAN and the central bank within the applicable reporting term; funds shall not be released to external escrow until the registration is complete.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for salvage and towage operations shall use SWIFT MT103 for direct payments to port agents, bunker suppliers, insurers, and crew-payroll processors. SWIFT MT202 is used for interbank cover transfers when the beneficiary instructs payment through a correspondent bank. For large salvage awards or time-charter payments involving a security mechanism, a Commercial Documentary Letter of Credit (L/C) under ICC UCP 600 is acceptable, with the local bank issuing or confirming the L/C. All outbound payments must be supported by underlying invoices and, where applicable, a DIAN foreign-exchange declaration; the SAS may maintain foreign-currency accounts abroad for voyage disbursements provided that repatriation to Colombia occurs at the end of the six-month service cycle. Payments to non-resident offshore escrow accounts for contractual security (e.g., Lloyds Standard Form) must be routed through a fully-approved correspondent bank and reported to the regulatory authority as part of the annual FX reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: COP/USD foreign-exchange forward contracts (FXDF) executed with locally authorized commercial banks for operational receipts and vendor payments.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on the USD/COP benchmark executed with non-resident banks, subject to Banco de la República registration when applied to a physical underlying contract.
Vanilla over-the-counter USD/COP call and put options used strictly for treasury hedging of segment-forecast cash flows.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CIRS) between COP and USD for refinancing long-term ship-finance or capital expenditure obligations, conditional on prior central-bank approval and compliance with derivative-margin rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual mercantile registry renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Cámara de Comercio (commercial chamber of registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of each calendar year, covering the previous fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal penalties accrue daily; inability to obtain positive continuation certificates; after repeated non-renewal (usually five years), administrative strike-off from the commercial registry and dissolution of the S.A.S.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and shareholders' meeting minutes (Estados financieros y actas de asamblea)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company's statutory books and, when applicable, Superintendencia de Sociedades via the annual renewal report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting must be held within three months from the fiscal year-end (by March 31 for a December 31 year-end); minutes and financial statements must be recorded without delay
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the annual meeting or to record minutes renders corporate decisions unenforceable; Superintendencia de Sociedades may impose fines and require judicial convocation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual external-information and tax confirmation return (Información exógena)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during March-June on the date set by DIAN resolution (assigned according to the taxpayer's NIT and filing status)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties up to the greater of 1% of gross income or approximately COP 10,800,000 (about USD 2,600) per filing, adjusted; no public-contract eligibility while pending.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit (Revisor Fiscal) for S.A.S. whose total assets or gross income exceed 5,000 times the current monthly legal minimum wage (about COP 7.1 billion / USD 1.7 million in 2025), or that are otherwise controlled by the Superintendencia de Sociedades; audit also requires a certified public accountant under Colombian law.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Full IFRS as adopted in Colombia by Law 1314 of 2009 for Group 1; simplified 'NIIF para las Pymes' for Group 2 (SMEs); historical-cost books in the functional currency Colombian peso.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each annual renewal of the mercantile registry, the S.A.S. must confirm to the Cámara de Comercio the identity of all ultimate beneficial owners (natural persons holding, directly or indirectly, more than 5% of the equity or who exercise de facto control); any transfer of shareholdings during the year, including changes from salvage-towage co-investors or vessel-owning entities, must be evidenced and the UBO register updated accordingly.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Acciones)
Register of Directors and Officers (Libro de Registro de Junta Directiva)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de la Asamblea)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 – 1,800 per year for registered-office and resident corporate-agent services in Bogotá, Cartagena or Barranquilla
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – 9,000 for a certified Revisor Fiscal audit of a mid-sized offshore towage and salvage S.A.S. subject to statutory audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% general corporate income tax rate for CY2025 under Article 240 of the Colombian Tax Code (E.T.), applicable to Sociedades por Acciones Simplificada (S.A.S.).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No broad statutory tax holiday exists for newly incorporated S.A.S. entities. Fiscal incentives include the 50% deduction for research and development expenses, a 100% deduction for payroll taxes linked to employees with disabilities, and limited exemption under Article 16 E.T. for income derived from international maritime towage or salvage when the operator demonstrates actual vessel ownership, Colombian manning, and substantive economic activity outside Colombian territorial waters. A 100% income exclusion for export services under Law 1607/2012 may apply only if the towage/salvage service is rendered exclusively to a foreign beneficiary and does not generate taxable income within Colombian territory; the operator must obtain and file the DIAN export-services certificate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 110 (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios). Filed electronically through the DIAN Muisca web portal (PIDE) or via DIAN-authorized electronic filing software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The filing deadline is set by an annual DIAN Resolution and is staggered according to the last digit of the taxpayer's NIT (tax identification number). For calendar-year 2025 filings, the return is due in the first filing period (generally April-May 2026) for entities with NITs ending in a low digit; large taxpayers and those with foreign parent entities are included in earlier tiers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rentas brutas ordinarias: gross revenues, including invoiced towage and salvage fees, wreck recovery payments, and standby towing contracts earned worldwide.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Colombian resident S.A.S. is taxed on worldwide gross income; the return must include all income earned from foreign principals even when funds are wired from outside Colombia. A foreign-owned branch or permanent establishment files Form 110 under its own NIT and reports only Colombia-sourced income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Egresos del exterior: deductible operational expenditures, including bunker fuel, crew wages, port call costs, towage equipment, insurance premiums, and salvage subcontractor fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only real, economically borne expenses that are connected to income generation. Management fees or group charges must be substantiated by a transfer-pricing study; otherwise DIAN will disallow the deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rentas exentas y no constitutivas de renta: items such as the export-services exclusion, dividends received from Colombian subsidiaries to the extent permitted, and the international maritime-traffic exemption, where evidenced.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not entitled to claim these lines directly. The Colombian entity must preserve the underlying official contracts, vessel registration documents, and DIAN approval before applying exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Renta líquida ordinaria: taxable base after deductions, exemptions, and inflation adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Computed identically for wholly foreign-owned S.A.S.; the entity is the taxpayer and cannot invoke the non-resident status of its beneficial owner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Impuesto básico de renta: gross corporate income tax computed at 35% on the net taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No percentage reduction applies merely because the shareholder is non-resident. Credit is given only for withholding taxes paid abroad creditable under a double tax agreement or Colombian unilateral credit rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a surcharge of 5% of the tax due for each month or fraction of a month of delay, capped at 100% of the tax due, with a floor of 10 UVT. Late tax payment accrues monthly interest on arrears (currently 2.1% per month). Incorrect or false information triggers penalties of 20-30% of the omitted value under Article 648 E.T. Failure to attach mandatory transfer-pricing documentation adds separate penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on gross dividends paid to non-resident shareholders on profits already subject to corporate income tax in Colombia (Article 242-1 E.T.). If the distributing entity has not paid the full 35% on the underlying profit due to an exemption, an additional tax of up to 35% may be assessed at distribution. A 5% treaty rate is common under an applicable double tax agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To benefit from a reduced dividend withholding rate under a DTA, the non-resident shareholder must (i) provide a certificate of tax residence (TRC) issued by the foreign competent authority for the calendar year in which the dividend is paid, (ii) deliver a formal declaration in Spanish to the Colombian withholding agent confirming beneficial ownership and residency, and (iii) file the corresponding administrative relief form with DIAN before or at the moment of the distribution. If excess WHT is withheld, the foreign shareholder must request a refund through DIAN's electronic refunds channel within two years under Article 850 E.T., attaching the TRC and evidence of place of effective management.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents are subject to a domestic withholding rate of 33%, with treaty rates typically 10-15% when the beneficial owner is resident in a DTA jurisdiction. Interest paid on ordinary foreign debt is withheld at 15%; interest paid to foreign banks for external credits may be exempt if registered with the Central Bank; treaty rates on interest are commonly 5-10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File preparation applies for taxable year 2025 when the taxpayer's gross income exceeds COP 4,183 million (84,000 UVT), or when total consolidated group revenue exceeds COP 400 billion, or when cross-border related-party transactions exceed COP 230 million per counterparty. The transfer-pricing return (Form 120) and documentation forms (Form 115 Master File and Form 116 Local File) must be filed with DIAN when any of these thresholds is met.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not have a Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulation (ESR); however, economic substance is enforced through the general anti-avoidance rule in Article 869 E.T., the abuse-of-corporate-form doctrine under Law 1258/2008, and the effective-beneficial-owner condition in every DTA. A Colombian S.A.S. holding foreign towage and salvage contracts must demonstrate actual business substance: vessel ownership on the Colombian flag or registered under DIMAR, substantive crew payroll, Colombian board decisions, local bank accounts, and quotidian operational management in Colombia. If the S.A.S. is wholly foreign-owned and merely passes income from foreign wreck-removal contracts without real local control, DIAN and DIMAR may re-characterize the entity as a fictious shell, reallocating its income to the foreign parent under transfer-pricing rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting or under-reporting gross revenue from international towage, salvage awards under Lloyd's Form, or emergency wreck-removal fees; booking revenue to an offshore affiliate not carrying the real economic risk; or deducting fictious bunker and subcontractor expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 340 of Law 1819/2016, tax evasion carries imprisonment of 4 to 9 years and a fine of 100% to 200% of the evaded tax. DIAN additionally imposes a penalty of 20% or 30% of the omitted income under Article 648 E.T., plus monthly arrears interest on the additional tax assessed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative and abandonment-partner of the S.A.S. are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax under Article 794 E.T. Criminal conviction triggers personal travel bans, disqualification from serving as legal representative of any Colombian commercial company, and civil restitution for the full tax deficiency and public-credit losses. In severe cases, the director may be summoned to an extradition-proceedings precautionary detention.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abuse of Corporate Form
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the S.A.S. as a mailbox entity with no employees, no vessel ownership, no board sessions, no Colombian bank account, and no contracts physically executed or administrated from Colombia; using the S.A.S. solely to channel foreign salvage fees to a non-resident shareholder at preferential rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A judge may pierce the corporate veil under the S.A.S. law (Law 1258/2008) and hold the shareholder and administrators personally liable for the company's obligations. DIAN can disregard the entity for income tax purposes, recharacterize all removed income as taxable to the foreign shareholder, and impose a penalty equal to 100% of the corrected tax. DIMAR may revoke the entity's towage and salvage operating license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil lifting directly exposes directors and shareholders to unlimited civil liability for the S.A.S.'s tax debts, contract liabilities, and salvage-related tort claims. A director convicted of misuse of corporate form faces a five-year prohibition on managing companies, judicial embargo of personal assets, and an exit ban until all DIAN claims are guaranteed or paid.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare or file the Colombian Transfer-Pricing Documentation for intercompany hull insurance, salvage fees paid to a related offshore towage pool, group overhead allocations, or loans from the foreign parent; alternatively submitting a comparability analysis with unrelated-market data but without functional and risk assessment for the towage and salvage operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 260-10 E.T., a penalty of 5% of the transaction value (minimum 10 UVT) applies for each materially incorrect or unfiled transfer-pricing declaration. Failure to submit the documentation allows DIAN to make a primary adjustment and add the 35% tax on the adjusted income plus a 20% penalty on the under-stated tax and monthly arrears interest. Manifestly false documentation can attract criminal penalties for fraudulent declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and tax advisors who sign or endorse false transfer-pricing studies are jointly liable for the adjusted tax and penalties under Article 260-10 E.T. Criminal indictment for aggravated tax fraud can follow if the false documentation is used to shift more than COP 1,000 million of taxable income. Personal liability includes disgorgement of the tax benefit, civil fines, and disqualification from serving as director of any Colombian-regulated financial or maritime entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving towage and salvage settlement proceeds in cash, through shell banks, or through intermediaries lacking beneficial-owner identification; failing to file a suspicious transaction report (ROS) with the Financial Information and Analysis Unit (UIAF) for unusual over-priced wire transfers; failing to adopt a proper AML/LAFT compliance manual for medium-risk maritime commercial activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under Law 526/1999 and UIAF Circulars can reach up to 2,500 monthly legal minimum wages (over COP 3.2 billion for 2025). DIMAR may suspend the towage vessel registration and revoke the coastal towage and salvage concession. If funds are linked to drug trafficking or organized crime, the Colombian antioffshore asset-forfeiture Law 1708/2014 authorizes seizure of the S.A.S.'s bank accounts and vessels.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly or recklessly ignore AML controls face a personal penalty of 5 to 10 years imprisonment, travel bans, and a lifetime prohibition on managing maritime or financial-activity companies. Additionally, the director may be subjected to asset forfeiture proceedings and required to pay civil restitution for all laundered gross proceeds attributable to the towage and salvage contracts.
